newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X edges higher, eye on Busang contracts.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X edges higher, eye on Busang contracts.

text.p: Shares in Bre-X Minerals Ltd edged higher on Tuesday, extending a modest recovery from Friday's selloff as the Canadian gold prospector awaited the signing of contracts of work for two sections of the Busang gold discovery in Indonesia.

Bre-X was up 0.15 at 15.85 on mid-afternoon turnover of 1.7 million shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange after adding 0.50 on Monday. The stock sank to a 52-week low of 14.25 in Toronto on Friday, depressed by an Indonesian newspaper report that questioned the size and viability of the deposit.
On Nasdaq, Bre-X was up 1/8 at 11-1/2 on Tuesday.
Indonesia's director general of mining Kuntoro Mangkusubroto said on Tuesday the government was still processing contracts of work for two sections of the Busang site in East Kalimantan province.
"We are still processing (Busang II and III) but they have not yet been approved by President Suharto," Kuntoro told reporters.
Kuntoro added he did not know when they would be ready.
Busang II contains the bulk of the gold discovered so far on the property, estimated by Bre-X at 71 million ounces of gold. There has been little exploration of Busang III.
Kuntoro said Suharto had approved 68 other contracts of work not connected with Busang.
Bre-X spokesman Richard Wool said the company had not heard from the Indonesian government about the Busang II and III contracts.
"On the COWs (contracts of work), the company has not received any official notice," Wool said in a telephone interview on Tuesday.
Analysts said the recent volatility in Bre-X stock appeared over as investors waited for Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc to complete its due diligence of the site.

"I think everybody is just waiting to find out what's going to happen. It's all quiet on the Western front until there are additional drill results that confirm or don't confirm the deposit," said one analyst.

Freeport has a 15 percent stake in Busang and is conducting its due diligence before developing a mine. An Indonesian newspaper last week quoted unnamed sources as saying that Freeport has come up with smaller numbers than Bre-X's estimates of Busang.
Freeport has said it will not comment on the review until it is completed.
Bre-X, which has a 45 percent stake in Busang, has vigorously denied the newspaper report and threatened to take legal action against certain parties and publications.
The remaining 40 percent in Busang is owned by the Indonesian government and two Indonesian companies.
